annotation.title_clean: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.authors_or_issuer: IOS Press (Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, vol. 366)
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366: Social Robots in Social Institutions (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Abstract of a conference paper applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor to workplace robotics. It uses his three social pathologies (forced division of labor, excessive division of labor, anomie) as a framework to analyze social and ethical impacts of robots and to outline socially responsible innovation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's theory of division of labor applies to robotics innovation
Three pathologies (forced, excessive division of labor, anomie) frame robot workplace impacts
Robots may contribute to disruptions in the shift from mechanical to organic solidarity
Proposes socially responsible innovation informed by Durkheim
